purpose: Phase 1B coordinator closure of the R-1 v1 architecture scope without converting future-residency measurement or absent runtime-confinement evidence into a paper seal.
scopeRule: The R-1 claim closed here is the v1 process and component floor. It does not claim that a resident host ships, that residency is valuable, or that language/process boundaries deny ambient authority at runtime.

v1Architecture.initialTopology: one-shot Rust orchestration host + pure data-only evaluation core
v1Architecture.coreBoundary: evaluate(stageInput: SealedStageInput, deps: CoreDeps, attempt: AttemptMetadata) -> CoreCompletion
hostOwns: storage publication and authoritative Run seal
coreOwns: policy evaluation over findings and exact Coverage
coreForbids: filesystem, network, spawn, clock, entropy, environment, storage, or provider handles in CoreDeps
Run sealing, publication, or termination mapping
v1Architecture.authoritativeRule: Warm state is never an evidence authority. Any future lifetime mode is prohibited from changing PlanId, exact Coverage semantics, EvidenceDigest, Run sealing, or HostTermination for identical semantic inputs.

v1Exclusions.reentryRule: A resident host requires target-workload measurement, an explicit product scope change, and LN-10 composition evidence. It is not an implementation option inside the v1 floor.

excludes: claims that the pure-core signature or package boundary is a security sandbox
v1Exclusions.reentryRule: Capability-dependent modes require a named restricted runtime and negative escape tests over direct, transitive, dynamic, native, and collaborator reach.

implementationEvidence.rule: The binding types and conformance obligations are architecture-complete. implementable:true means a test can be built; it does not establish that the Rust implementation passed it.
requiredLater: LN-01 through LN-11 and LN-13 through LN-14 execution records against the product
negative controls for every claimed conformance property
LN-10 only if a resident topology is proposed after v1
neverRequiredForArchitectureFreeze: LN-12 while capability-dependent modes remain excluded

findingDispositions.reasoning: The binding has one boundary: SealedStageInput to CoreCompletion. Fact derivation and Run sealing are host-owned.
findingDispositions.verification: check-r1.py rejects restored SealedRun and fact-derivation-in-core mutations.

findingDispositions.reasoning: CoreDeps is a closed data-only record and the core never calls an effectful port.
findingDispositions.verification: check-r1.py rejects StorePort permission and CoreDeps removal.

findingDispositions.reasoning: CoreCompletion carries the policy identity, verdict, and derivation digest needed by host sealing.
Unexecuted tests specify obligations; LN-12 cannot discharge or close runtime authority.
findingDispositions.verification: check-r1.py rejects both runtime discharge through LN-12 and DISCHARGED without QUALIFIED/DEMONSTRATED evidence.

findingDispositions.reasoning: LN-10 is composition acceptance, not evidence about the host suite alone.
findingDispositions.verification: check-r1.py rejects assigning LN-10 to the host suite.

findingDispositions.reasoning: Attempt identity is host-injected metadata, and the core has no entropy input.
findingDispositions.verification: check-r1.py rejects reintroduced entropy and core-owned ExecutionId.

findingDispositions.reasoning: The v1 build has one topology: one-shot host plus pure core. Future residency is excluded and parked, so no week-one topology fork remains.
findingDispositions.verification: check-r1.py rejects loss of the one-shot floor and loss of the closure's v1 residency exclusion.

forbiddenInferences: SEAL-WITH-CHANGES does not mean R-1 product conformance is DEMONSTRATED.
The absence of effectful fields from CoreDeps is not runtime capability denial.
A future resident host is not permitted to appear behind a v1 flag or alternate code path.
The core never produces SealedRun and the host never re-evaluates policyOutcome.

set.title: V1 execution uses a one-shot orchestration host and lifetime-neutral pure evaluation core
set.note: Phase 1B coordinator closure: SEAL-WITH-CHANGES for the v1 one-shot host + pure data-only evaluation core. Resident/autostart/default/multi-project modes are parked outside v1. Runtime ambient-authority denial remains NOT DISCHARGED on ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT, and dependent authority modes are excluded. Implementable conformance tests specify later product evidence; they do not demonstrate it.
nonBlockingResiduals: R1-PARK-RESIDENCY — resident-host value and topology are parked outside v1; reentry requires measurement and product scope change
R1-PARK-RUNTIME-DENIAL — runtime ambient-authority denial is NOT DISCHARGED; capability-dependent modes remain excluded on ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT
parkedExclusions: runtime-confinement claim and every authority mode that depends on it
implementationEvidencePending: Implementation must produce retained conformance evidence; this is release/implementation qualification, not an architecture blocker.

claimRegisterPatch.dependencyRationale: The v1 R-1 scope retracts runtime denial and excludes dependent modes rather than relying on ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT.

knownLimitations: The product does not yet exist, so no R-1 implementation property is demonstrated.
The original Reviewer 2 LN-10 suite-assignment sub-review was not blind; the repaired structural assignment is checker-enforced.
This closure deliberately makes no claim about whether a resident host should ever ship.

sealRecommendation.note: Seal the one-shot/pure-core v1 architecture. Carry residency and runtime denial as named non-blocking parks, not seal blockers and not demonstrated claims.
sealRecommendation.consumerB: Implement exactly one v1 topology. Do not invent resident mode, effectful core ports, SealedRun-from-core, or a runtime-confinement claim.
